title: Needleburst quantile scratchpad
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad to capture an experiment series I ran to investigate very-short, very-high-amplitude arrival bursts (what I'm calling "needles") that disproportionately inflate p99/p999. Want to capture setup, raw observations, a couple of cheap visualizations, and next steps before I forget details.

Background / hypothesis:
- We see periodic microspikes in p99 that are not explained by long-running requests or large payloads.
- Hypothesis: sub-100ms arrival clusters cause skewed batching behavior + cache churn. A single heavyweight batch can block a stream of small requests and create long tails.

Environment / harness:
- Model under test: redwood/gamma-7b-8k (quantized eval build, int8-path enabled).
- Hardware: single A100-40G equivalent (dedicated pool node in local dev cluster), CUDA 12 stack, runtime v1.13.2-dev.
- Serving config (baseline): concurrency=8, batch_window_ms=2, max_batch_tokens=2048, kv_cache_enabled=true, preemption=false.
- Traffic generator: local asyncio runner (scripts/needleburst-runner.py). Pattern = Poisson baseline + superimposed needle bursts (sharp gaussian-like bursts). Baseline QPS: 150. Needle bursts: amplitude 800-1200 QPS peak, duration 30-60ms, inter-arrival 7-12s. Payload token distribution: 16/64/128 tokens (mix 60/30/10).
- Metrics collected: request latency (client-observed), server enqueue time, batch size, GPU kernel durations, kv_cache_hit (boolean), in-flight count. Exported traces + histogram snapshots.

Quick run notes (command):
- python3 scripts/needleburst-runner.py --model gamma-7b --qps 150 --needle-peaks 1000 --needle-width-ms 40 --run-seconds 120 --out ./runs/run-20250212-01.json
- Server run: ./serve --config conf/needle-default.yaml --telemetry=trace,summaries

Raw numbers (baseline config, single run):
- baseline throughput: stable around 150 qps (except bursts)
- median latency (p50): 18 ms
- p95: 42 ms
- p99: 143 ms
- p999: 342 ms
- average batch size: 10 tokens per batch during baseline, spikes to 62 during needles
- kv_cache_hit rate: baseline ~84%, during needles drops to ~67%

Notes on trace inspection:
- The p99/p999 spikes align tightly with needle windows. Individual slow requests show ~60-120ms of waiting in server queue while a large batch executes.
- Kernel durations are not the root cause: long tail comes from waiting + serialization of batch formation (big-batch blocks small ones).
- Observed cases where a small request enters while a large batch forms and its latency becomes dominated by the tail of that batch.

Needleplot (very rough ascii time-series of 5ms buckets during a needle):
(time buckets -> requests)
[ 0ms: ||||||||||||||| ]  (baseline 8 qps equivalent)
[ 5ms: |||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||| ] (superpeak)
[10ms: |||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||| ]
[15ms: |||||||| ]
[20ms: ||| ]

Experiment matrix tried (short):
1) batch_window_ms: 1 / 2 / 5 / 10
2) concurrency: 4 / 8 / 12 / 16
3) max_batch_tokens: 2048 / 4096 / 8192
4) warm-cache vs forced-cold resets before run
5) ingress shaping: leaky-bucket token-burst limits (burst=200/500), token refill 150 qps
6) prefix caching toggles / kv cache warmup scripts

Selected results summary (best-effort, averaged across 3 runs each):
- batch_window_ms=1: p99 dropped from 143 -> 103 ms (-28%), p999 342 -> 270 ms (-21%). Downsides: GPU utilization dropped ~6% (smaller batches).
- batch_window_ms=10: p99 increased to ~185 ms (bigger batches forming), higher efficiency but worse tail.
- concurrency=16 with batch_window_ms=2: p50 shifted up slightly (18 -> 22 ms) but p99 improved to ~95 ms. Interpretation: parallelism helps small-request starvation but increases baseline latency due to scheduling overhead.
- max_batch_tokens=4096: little change vs 2048 in median, slightly better p999 in chaotic runs (maybe reduces fraction of cross-batch blocking).
- kv_cache warmup: Prewarming with 1k warmup chats (script warmup/kvcache_seed.py) improved p99 by ~15% during repeated-pattern needles.
- ingress shaping (burst token cap 200): p999 improved by ~40% (342 -> ~205 ms) but baseline p50 added ~3 ms due to enforced smoothing.

Interpretation / trade-offs:
- The tail is dominated by queueing/ordering effects, not raw kernel time. Controls that reduce cross-request interference (more concurrency lanes, shorter batch windows, or smoothing ingress) lower the tail.
- There's no free lunch: reducing batch window eats into GPU efficiency. Increasing concurrency buys tail reduction at cost of p50 and some overhead.
- KV cache warmup helps for repetitive contexts (chat), but for cold or very diverse requests it doesn't help much.

Immediate suggestions (practical):
- For Dedicated profile targeted at interactive apps with occasional needles, consider default: batch_window_ms=2, concurrency=12, max_batch_tokens=4096, kvcache_prewarm=true. Rationale: balances p50 and stabilizes p99.
- Add a Canary job that replays needleburst traffic pattern against new runtime builds to catch regressions. Put harness under repro-harness PR linked above.
- Expose a "needle-detection" metric in Console: detect short high-amplitude spikes and report correlation with p99 changes (small metric, high signal).
- SRE ticket: INF-4921 (create fleet shadow job to run needlebursts weekly on a small slice).

To-do / follow-ups (me):
- [ ] Run longer-duration (1h) runs to validate steady-state impact of shaping.
- [ ] Try hybrid window: dynamic batch_window_ms that shrinks when small-request fraction rises. Prototype: runtime flag dynamic_batch=true.
- [ ] Add microtrace capture automatically for requests exceeding 2x p95 during needles and upload to GH issue.
- [ ] Share top-line numbers with Priya + SRE in #serving-runtime tomorrow.

Random observations (notes-to-self):
- There were occasional outliers where a single failed kernel requeue caused a tail > 1s; rare but needs monitoring.
- Thought: we should consider a "fast-lane" scheduler for short-token requests (<32 tokens) to reduce being trapped by big-batches. Worth prototyping as a runtime scheduler tweak.

Files / commands I used / scripts to copy into reproducible folder:
- scripts/needleburst-runner.py (traffic generator)
- conf/needle-default.yaml (server config)
- warmup/kvcache_seed.py
- runs/run-20250212-01.json (raw trace + histogram)

End — saving this before I start the longer runs. Will link results to INF-4921 and PR once I have longer-run numbers.

Zarina
